Its Li-rich composition should also keep the interface from being a Li-ion blocker.

proposals.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap, insulating Li-containing oxide and the best-known protective coating for LiCoO2 at 4 V. Its Nb5+ is more oxidized and less basic than the Zr/P/B routes already tried, so it may avoid the La-containing byproducts (LaPO4, LaBO3, La2Zr2O7) seen at the LLZO contact. The main risk is that Nb can still form La-Nb-O phases with LLZO, so the contact penalty needs checking.

Its high Li content should also keep the interface Li-ion permeable and reduce the Li-blocking seen in the Li-poor coatings.

proposals.hypothesis: Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich zirconate that shares the Zr4+ cation with the LLZO electrolyte, so it should have a smaller chemical driving force to form La/Zr byproducts at the contact than the Al, Nb, P, B or F coatings tried so far. Its higher Li content than Li2ZrO3 may also keep the interface Li-ion permeable and reduce the Li-blocking seen in Li-poor coatings. It should be insulating and oxidatively stable near 4 V vs Li/LiCoO2.
proposals.motivation: Li2ZrO3 (mp-aaaaagdw) gave the Zr-oxide contact penalty of about 0.044 eV/atom at the LLZO interface, while its self-decomposition penalty (0.35) was high. Li6Zr2O7 keeps the Zr-O chemistry but moves to a more Li-rich composition, to test whether the self-decomposition penalty can be lowered while the contact penalty stays low.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich phosphate with high oxidative stability at about 4 V vs Li. It is chemically compatible with both LLZO and LiCoO2 and is a established interfacial coating for reducing cathode-electrolyte reactions and interdiffusion. Its Li-rich composition should also keep the interface from being a Li-ion blocker.

Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich borate. Its high Li content should avoid the Li-ion blocking seen in the Li3PO4 contact products. Borate frameworks are less likely than phosphates to form La/Zr phosphate and oxide byproducts at the LLZO contact, so the contact penalty may fall below the 0.05 eV/atom threshold.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with band gap 5.7 eV and self-decomposition penalty 0.002, but its LLZO contact penalty of 0.099 eV/atom (bin 4) failed the 0.05 threshold because it decomposes to LaPO4, ZrO2 and O2.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, insulating lithium zirconate. Its Zr is already in the LLZO lattice, so it should have a smaller driving force to form La/Zr phosphate and oxide byproducts at the LLZO contact than the phosphate or borate coatings tried so far, which both gave La-containing products. It is an oxide that should be stable against LiCoO2 at about 4 V, and it is a known protective coating family for cathodes. Its Li content is lower than the Li-rich candidates, so it may be a weaker Li-ion conductor, but it avoids the phosphorus and boron routes that produced the LaPO4 and LaBO3 contact products.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) gave a large penalty of 0.313 (bin 15) with Co and La byproducts. Li3BO3 (mp-aaaabojb) was insulating and stable, but its LLZO contact still gave LaPO4, ZrO2 and O2 with penalty 0.099 (bin 4). Both failures involve La/Zr byproducts, so a Zr-bearing oxide is a different chemical family to test.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap, insulating Li-containing oxide and the best-known protective coating for LiCoO2 at 4 V. Its Nb5+ is more oxidized and less basic than the Zr/P/B routes already tried, so it may avoid the La-containing byproducts (LaPO4, LaBO3, La2Zr2O7) seen at the LLZO contact. The main risk is that Nb can still form La-Nb-O phases with LLZO, so the contact penalty needs checking.
proposal.motivation: Li2ZrO3 (mp-aaaaagdw) was insulating with band gap 5.7 eV, but its LLZO contact still formed LaPO4 and ZrO2 with penalty 0.099 (bin 4). Li3PO4 and Li3BO3 also gave La-containing products with larger penalties. A Nb-based oxide tests a different transition-metal chemistry at the LLZO interface.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich fluoride with very high oxidative stability at about 4 V vs Li, so it should not decompose on the LiCoO2 side. Fluoride anions are less basic and less reactive toward the La/Zr framework than phosphate, borate or Nb-oxide anions, so the LLZO contact should avoid the La-containing byproducts (LaPO4, LaBO3, LaNbO4) that drove the earlier penalties. It also keeps Li-ion transport through the interface, unlike a Li-deficient coating.
proposal.motivation: All four oxide, phosphate and borate coatings (Li3PO4, Li3BO3, Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3) formed La-containing products at the LLZO contact, with penalties of 0.082 to 0.313 eV/atom. The fluoride family has not been tested yet.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, insulating, Li-containing oxide and a known protective coating for LiCoO2 at 4 V. Al3+ is a hard, weakly basic cation that is less prone than Zr, Nb, or P to forming La-containing byproducts with LLZO. The main risk is that Al can still form La-Al-O or Li-rich aluminate phases at the LLZO contact, so the contact penalty needs checking.
proposal.motivation: Li2ZrO3 (mp-aaaaagdw) and LiNbO3 (mp-aaaaafnn) were insulating and stable, with the lowest contact penalties so far (about 0.08 to 0.10, bin 4). Both still formed LaNbO4, LaPO4, or ZrO2 byproducts. Switching the cation to Al3+ tests whether the La/Zr-oxide driving force can be reduced within the oxide family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4SiO4 is a wide-gap, insulating, Li-rich orthosilicate. Si4+ is a small, highly charged, weakly basic cation with little tendency to form La-containing phases, so the LLZO contact may avoid the LaPO4, LaBO3, LaNbO4 and LaF3 byproducts that drove earlier penalties. Its high Li content should also keep the interface Li-ion permeable and reduce the Li-blocking seen in the Li-poor coatings.

The silicate family has not been tested, and the Li-rich orthosilicate is the most Li-rich chemistry not yet sampled in this family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3AlF6 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating fluoride.
